rounds.text: The rules-based screen awards QMS Medical Allied Services Ltd a strong BUY score of 86 out of 100, underpinned by robust fundamental growth highlights including year-on-year sales growth of 22% and net profit growth of 25% [E53, E54, E56]. This operational momentum translates into stellar cash generation, with operating and free cash flows reaching Rs 19 Cr in March 2026, delivering an elite cash conversion ratio of 1.58x that proves profits are fully backed by hard cash [E24, E25, E26]. Furthermore, the company outpaces sector benchmarks on capital efficiency with a ROCE of 12.91% compared to the sector's 11.76%, while trading at an attractive EV/EBITDA of 14.58x against a higher sector benchmark of 16.21x [E10, E11]. Market participants are increasingly recognizing this value proposition, as evidenced by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, a surging twelve-month price return of 78.1%, and a technical posture where the price comfortably sits above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40, E41, E42]. Institutional confidence is also quietly building, highlighted by domestic institutions increasing their stake by 1.30 percentage points and generating a positive money flow signal [E33, E34]. Conceded: [E35], [E36], [E52].

The current market price of ₹ 172 leaves no margin of safety, trading at a negative margin of -12.5% against a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 153 per share [E35, E36]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price implies an 11.6% earnings growth, which outpaces the 10.0% growth assumed in the base case [E37]. Leverage is also on the rise, with borrowings increasing to Rs 74 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 60 Cr a year earlier [E29]. Insider alignment is weakening as well, evidenced by promoter holding dropping by 5.56 percentage points from 73.67% in Dec 2022 to 68.11% in Sep 2026 [E31]. Finally, the stock carries severe downside risks for holders, demonstrated by a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -68.5% and an annualized volatility of 62.0% [E43, E44]. Conceded: [E41].

While the bear flags a negative margin of safety under a DCF model [E35, E36], the rules-based screen firmly scores the business at 86 out of 100 with a buy signal, supported by strong YoY sales growth of 22% and net profit growth of 25% [E53, E54, E56]. Conceded: [E37]. Although borrowings increased to Rs 74 Cr [E29], the company generated robust operating and free cash flow of Rs 19 Cr in March 2026 with a high cash conversion ratio of 1.58x, proving that reported profits are fully backed by actual cash [E24, E25, E26]. Conceded: [E31]. Regarding promoter holding changes [E31], domestic institutional investors have stepped in by increasing their stake to 1.30% alongside a positive institutional money flow signal [E33, E34]. Finally, the stock's historical volatility and drawdown [E43, E44] are countered by extraordinary relative strength of 100 against the Nifty 500, a twelve-month price return of 78.1%, and a technical position where the price sits comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40, E41, E42].

Conceded: [E53], [E54], [E56]. Despite the rules-based screen score, the fundamental valuation framework reveals that a discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at Rs 153 per share against a market price of Rs 172, delivering a negative margin of safety of -12.5% [E35, E36]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price demands an 11.6% earnings growth rate, which surpasses the base case assumption of 10.0% and exposes the valuation to downside if expectations cool [E37]. While the bull highlights operating cash flow of Rs 19 Cr [E25], borrowings simultaneously escalated to Rs 74 Cr from Rs 60 Cr in the prior year [E29]. Conceded: [E33], [E34]. Countering the narrative of institutional support, promoter holding has eroded by 5.56 percentage points down to 68.11%, and foreign institutional holdings have similarly dropped [E31, E32]. Finally, while the bull celebrates price momentum, the historical record shows an extreme annualised volatility of 62.0% and a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -68.5% [E43, E44], complemented by a price-led signal indicating that recent price growth outpaces profit growth by 94% with expectations running ahead of delivery [E47].

While the bear highlights a negative margin of safety in the discounted cash flow model [E36], the company actually trades at a P/E of 26.44x, which is a discount to the sector benchmark of 31.05x [E6], and its EV/EBITDA of 14.58x is more attractive than the sector's 16.21x [E11]. The concern that the market expects 11.6% growth [E37] is mitigated by the fact that the company is currently delivering far higher performance, with sales up 22% YoY [E54] and net profit growing at 25% YoY [E56, E57]. Conceded: [E29]; however, the increase in borrowings is balanced by a robust cash conversion ratio of 1.58x [E24] and Rs 19 Cr in free cash flow [E26], supporting a manageable debt-to-equity ratio of 0.71x [E27]. Conceded: [E31, E32, E52]; yet the decline in promoter and foreign holdings is countered by the entry of domestic institutions, which grew from 0.00% to 1.30% [E33], resulting in a positive institutional money flow signal [E34]. Despite historical volatility and drawdowns [E43, E44], the stock demonstrates elite market leadership with a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E41] and a strong technical profile where the price remains above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40]. While price growth has outpaced profit growth recently [E47], the company's capital efficiency remains superior to its peers, with an ROCE of 12.91% exceeding the sector benchmark of 11.76% [E10].

The bull leans on a discounted P/E of 26.44x and EV/EBITDA of 14.58x [E6, E11], but ignores that the intrinsic valuation model explicitly points to a negative margin of safety of -12.5% [E35, E36]. While the bull cites robust 22% sales growth and 25% net profit growth [E54, E56, E57], trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth actually sits at -15% [E15], revealing a stark divergence in performance timeframes. Conceded: [E24, E26, E27]; however, borrowings still expanded to Rs 74 Cr from Rs 60 Cr [E29] while the current ratio of 1.56x offers only an adequate but thin liquidity buffer [E28]. Conceded: [E33, E34]; nevertheless, promoter ownership has dropped by 5.56 percentage points to 68.11% [E31] and foreign institutional holdings have similarly declined [E32]. Finally, the reliance on high relative-strength and moving averages [E40, E41] masks extreme volatility of 62.0% [E44] and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -68.5% [E43], exposing long-term holders to severe risk.
